title: Triple treble — the tall one for lace arches
subtitle: Three entry yarn-overs, five loops closed one pair at a time
excerpt: Triple treble (UK trtr) is the tallest common crochet stitch. Three yarn-overs on entry produce five loops on the hook, closed in pairs. It appears in deep lace arches, hairpin lace patterns, and the taller versions of fan and shell motifs.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776 — the triple treble in lace mesh and tall edging work. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 4 (1889) — tall stitch patterns in filet crochet.

glossaryTerms.definition: UK term for the tallest common crochet stitch: yarn over three times before inserting, pull up a loop (five loops on hook), then yarn over and pull through two loops four times. US patterns call this double treble.

heroPrompt: A small swatch of triple treble in DK cotton showing very tall open columns, compared side by side with a few rows of treble at half the height, on a wooden board.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: Five loops on hook before closing — the triple treble entry

content.text: extends the double treble one step further: three yarn-overs on entry, five loops on the hook after pulling up a loop, and four pairs to close. The stitch is very tall and open. In UK patterns the abbreviation is trtr; US patterns call the same stitch double treble (dtr).
Row 1: ch 5 (counts as first trtr). Yarn over three times, then insert hook into the 6th chain from the hook.
Yarn over and pull up a loop — five loops on the hook.
Yarn over and pull through two loops — four remain.
Yarn over and pull through two loops — three remain.
Yarn over and pull through two loops — two remain.
Yarn over and pull through the final two loops. One trtr made.
Work 1 trtr in each chain across — 12 trtr including the ch-5. Turn.

attrs.title: The pattern for tall stitches
attrs.body: Every stitch above the treble follows the same pattern: one more entry yarn-over, one more loop on the hook, one more close stage. Triple treble: 3 entry yo, 5 loops, 4 closes. Quadruple treble: 4 entry yo, 6 loops, 5 closes. The rule of 'always two at a time, tip first' applies throughout.

items.symptom: Entry yarn-overs slide down the hook before inserting
items.cause: The three loops bunch toward the tip on slippery yarn
items.fix: Hold all three yarn-over loops firmly against the shaft before inserting. Grip the working yarn close to the hook to stop the loops sliding.

items.symptom: Stitch looks uneven — loops at different heights
items.cause: The three entry yarn-overs were made at different positions on the shaft
items.fix: Make all three yarn-overs at the same point on the shaft. They should form three even-size loops, not one big and two small.

content.text: Triple trebles appear in broomstick lace — the elongated loop hung on a dowel is related to this stitch height. Deep fan and shell stitches sometimes use triple treble for the outer petals. The crossed double treble pairs two dtr in reverse order for a tall X-stitch.
